Prelude – A Stable Galaxy of Relative Peace

Before contact, the occasional dispute over resources in the densely populated inner arms was common, but rarely damaged infrastructure or civilians and was monitored for breaches of the Conflict Protocols by Galactic Command species not engaged in the dispute.

Any action such as dishonorable conduct, unnecesarry force or targeting of civilians was subject to punishments ranging from fines to eradication of the offending force, depending on the severity of the breach. Rarely did the GC step in at this period of time, with such clear and immediate penalties having been known to all trained ship captains for millenia.

Expansion into the outer arms remained slow in progress, as the relative efficiency of stable trade was limited by the immense distances required between friendly ports the further one travelled from the galactic core.

Without access to a cleared shipping lane, FTL travel was impossible for cargo transport, even with the most expensive protection systems equipped, due to their immense mass and surface area protection required.

It simply drew too much fuel to be commercially viable for any but freighters of the rarest and most valuable elements and compounds not found in abundance in the Core systems, these extremely expensive vessels accompanied by a military force of the contracting species.

Beyond established shipping lanes, setup, monitored and protected by Galactic Command forces was the realm of scientists, resource explorers or poorer traders, all searching for new systems, sentients, life forms or mineral resources.

Smaller vessels could take advantage of FTL travel, yet none would dare without protection, leaving many to opt for gravity assisted auto-pilot, cheap electromagnetic propulsion and simple cryopods.

It wasn't a life many entered willingly, to join the ranks of deep spacers was to say goodbye to any loved lones of your previous life. For the lowest rungs of society, wishing a better life for their young, beyond joining a military force and typically dying in a pointless conflict that would be resolved by diplomatic intervention shortly after, there was little else on offer.

The risks remained the same, but militaries were far more discerning with their staffing compared to most ship captains of the outer arms.

This freedom of course drew pirates, slavers and other unsavoury types - taking full advantage of the lack of GC forces prying eyes to raid freighters and stations, conduct ethically questionable experiments for futher sale or bulk resource extraction with cheap, disposable enslaved sentients.

All groups had the same buyers market, however information was the biggest galactic commodity, but this didn't stop less scrupulous species from engaging in the illegal trade of sentients if they believed they could on the outer arms. With layers of protection afforded by shell companies and the like, it was more common than the GC Command admitted in any report.

A.I machines had many uses, but corporations had long since run the numbers and found the use of already adapted local species, occasionally enhanced if required, to attain minerals as being an economically superior option to shipping millions of expensive A.I units vast distances, many shipments often captured and resold to other species.

The locations of new rare minerals, compounds, sentient species or even exploitable new multi-cellular life always had immense value, sure many species in deep space could get by on just the scrap trade, but it was these new finds payouts that drew all lifeforms to dare traverse the voids of space.

If not for an odd bit of debris drifting into a cleared shipping lane, the galaxy may have remained at relative peace for perhaps a full Galactic year (~800,000 of their own 'Julian' years). No one could have predicted what our greed for knowledge and resources would unleash...
